# Alternatives Comparison

Dimension 5 of the frontend state management research. Compares TanStack Query +
Zustand against Redux Toolkit + RTK Query, Jotai, Recoil, Valtio, and going
all-in on TanStack Query.

See [citations.md](../citations.md) for full source details.

## Architectural Models

| Library | Model | State Location | Update Style |
|---------|-------|---------------|--------------|
| Zustand | Single store, top-down | External (module) | Immutable (set) |
| Jotai | Atomic, bottom-up | React tree (atoms) | Immutable (atom updates) |
| Valtio | Proxy-based | External (module) | Mutable (direct mutation) |
| Redux Toolkit | Single store, flux | External (module) | Immutable (reducers) |
| Recoil | Atomic, top-down | React tree (atoms + string keys) | Immutable | 

Source: [16] [17]

## Zustand vs Redux Toolkit

| Dimension | Zustand | Redux Toolkit |
|-----------|---------|---------------|
| Provider required | No | Yes (wraps app in context) |
| Boilerplate | Minimal | Moderate (slices, reducers) |
| DevTools | Via middleware | Built-in, comprehensive |
| Middleware ecosystem | Small (immer, persist, devtools) | Large (thunk, saga, listener) |
| Learning curve | Low | Moderate-high |
| Team governance | Convention-based | Pattern-enforced |
| Best for | Small-to-medium apps | Large teams (5+ devs) needing strict patterns |

Redux Toolkit remains dominant in enterprises requiring strict unidirectional
data flow, time-travel debugging, and middleware ecosystems [16]. It enforces
patterns critical for codebases with many engineers.

## Zustand vs Jotai

Both by Daishi Kato; different philosophies [16] [17]:

| Dimension | Zustand | Jotai |
|-----------|---------|-------|
| Mental model | Redux-like single store | Recoil-like atoms |
| Render optimization | Manual (selectors) | Automatic (atom dependencies) |
| Code splitting | Good (module-level stores) | Better (atoms are granular) |
| Suspense integration | Not built-in | Built-in |
| Context requirement | No | Optional (Provider for isolation) |
| Best for | Simple module-level state, Redux users | Fine-grained reactivity, useState+useContext migration |

Jotai official comparison: "Jotai is aiming for simplicity, minimalistic API
and can do much more than useContext" [17].

## Zustand vs Valtio

| Dimension | Zustand | Valtio |
|-----------|---------|-------|
| State model | Immutable | Mutable (proxy-based) |
| Update syntax | `set(s => ({ count: s.count + 1 }))` | `state.count += 1` |
| Render optimization | Manual (selectors) | Automatic (property access tracking) |
| React alignment | High (immutable matches React model) | Lower (mutable conflicts conceptually) |
| TypeScript | Excellent | Challenges with nested structures |
| Debugging | Predictable (immutable snapshots) | Harder (proxy indirection) |

Source: [16]

## Recoil: Deprecated

Recoil was **archived by Meta on January 1, 2025** [18]:

- Never left "experimental" status despite production use at Meta
- Douglas Armstrong (Meta, 2022): compatibility with React 18 concurrent
  features was the blocker [18]
- Community frustrated by indefinite experimental label deterring adoption
- No official migration path published
- **Recommended alternatives**: Jotai (closest API similarity), Zustand [17]

## TanStack Query vs RTK Query

| Feature | TanStack Query | RTK Query |
|---------|---------------|-----------|
| Framework | Agnostic (React, Vue, Solid, Svelte) | Redux-only |
| Infinite queries | Yes (bidirectional) | Limited |
| DevTools | Dedicated, visual | Redux DevTools (shared) |
| Bundle size | ~10 KB | Part of RTK (~14 KB total) |
| Cache model | Query key hierarchy | Endpoint + tag system |
| Background refetch | Smart triggers (mount, focus, reconnect) | Manual or tag-based |
| Existing Redux app | Separate addition | Seamless integration |

TanStack Query's official comparison table shows feature parity or advantage
over RTK Query in most categories [30]. RTK Query's strength is seamless
integration with existing Redux stores.

## Going All-In on TanStack Query

TanStack Query explicitly states it does **not** replace client state
management [2]. It manages server state — async cache that can become stale.

For apps where "remaining global client state is tiny" after moving API data
to Query (which Tanner Linsley observed at Nozzle [2]), useState + useContext
may suffice for client state without a dedicated library.

This works when:
- Client state is minimal (theme, auth token, maybe a sidebar toggle)
- No complex client-side workflows or editing state
- No need for state outside React (WebSocket managers, workers)

## Adoption Data

From search results referencing npm downloads and surveys [38]:

- Zustand: ~20M+ weekly npm downloads (as of early 2026)
- Redux Toolkit: ~10M weekly downloads
- TanStack Query: ~5-12M weekly downloads
- Jotai: Growing but smaller

Note: npm download numbers vary by source and timeframe. These are
approximate indicators of relative adoption, not precise measurements.

State of React 2025 survey shows Zustand as the user satisfaction leader [38].

## Decision Framework

| If you need... | Use... |
|----------------|--------|
| Server state management | TanStack Query |
| Simple client state (small-medium app) | Zustand |
| Atomic/fine-grained reactivity | Jotai |
| Strict team governance (10+ devs) | Redux Toolkit |
| Mutable state model | Valtio |
| Recoil replacement | Jotai |
| State outside React | Zustand (vanilla store) |

## Gaps and Limitations

- No rigorous performance benchmarks comparing re-render counts or memory usage
  across libraries
- npm download numbers are approximate and source-dependent
- Enterprise adoption data for Zustand vs Redux is largely anecdotal
- Migration effort estimates between solutions not quantified
